Bachelor of Science in Anesthesia Technology - Dubai Medical University
Program Overview

The Bachelor of Science in Anesthesia Technology (BS-ANTech) at Dubai Medical University is a four-year program designed to prepare highly skilled perioperative professionals who support anesthesia delivery, patient monitoring, and surgical safety. The curriculum combines strong foundations in biomedical sciences with specialized training in anesthesia systems, patient care technologies, and clinical practice in modern healthcare environments.

During the first two years, students build essential knowledge in anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pharmacology, and pathology, while developing professional competencies in communication, research, and healthcare ethics. Early exposure to perioperative care, sterility science, infection control, and anesthesia technology introduces students to the clinical environment.

In Year 3, the program advances into specialized anesthesia topics including patient monitoring, anesthesia equipment and safety systems, perioperative diagnostics, and anesthesia management across different surgical contexts. Simulation and laboratory training strengthen clinical decision-making and teamwork.

The final year focuses on advanced anesthesia practice and extensive supervised clinical training in operating rooms and perioperative units. Through these experiences, graduates develop the technical competence, critical thinking, and professional confidence needed to contribute effectively to multidisciplinary surgical teams and to support high standards of patient safety and care.

Bachelor of Science in Audiology and Speech Language Pathology - Dubai Medical University - College of Health Sciences

The Bachelor of Science in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (BS-ASLP) at Dubai Medical University is a four-year program designed to prepare professionals capable of assessing, diagnosing, and supporting individuals with speech, language, hearing, and swallowing disorders across the lifespan. The program integrates biomedical sciences, communication sciences, and clinical training to develop graduates who can contribute effectively to multidisciplinary healthcare and rehabilitation teams.

During the first two years, students build a strong scientific and academic foundation through courses in biology, chemistry, physics, anatomy and physiology, microbiology, pharmacology, pathology, and research methods. Students are introduced to the fundamentals of communication disorders, linguistics and phonetics, psychology, and language development, providing the essential knowledge required to understand speech, hearing, and human communication.

In Year 3, the curriculum progresses to specialized topics in speech-language pathology and audiology, including neuroscience of communication, voice and fluency disorders, motor speech disorders, school-age language disorders, bilingualism, hearing assessment, pediatric audiology, auditory processing disorders, and swallowing disorders. Laboratory sessions and applied training strengthen diagnostic and clinical reasoning skills.

The final year focuses on intensive supervised clinical practicum in both speech-language pathology and audiology, allowing students to apply assessment and intervention techniques in real clinical settings. The program concludes with a research project that develops analytical and evidence-based practice skills, preparing graduates for professional practice and further specialization in communication health sciences.

Bachelor of Science in Medical Imaging Sciences - Dubai Medical University - College of Health Sciences

The Bachelor of Science in Medical Imaging Sciences (BS-MIS) at Dubai Medical University is a four-year program designed to prepare competent imaging professionals who support the diagnosis and management of disease through advanced medical imaging technologies. The program combines strong foundations in biomedical sciences with specialized training in diagnostic imaging, radiation science, imaging equipment, and clinical practice in modern healthcare environments.

During the first two years, students develop essential knowledge in anatomy, physiology, biology, physics, and pathology, while also building competencies in communication, research, and healthcare ethics. Foundational courses introduce the principles of medical imaging, radiation physics, and patient care, preparing students for safe and effective practice in imaging environments.

In Year 3, the curriculum advances into specialized imaging disciplines, including radiographic techniques, imaging instrumentation, radiation protection, image processing, and quality assurance. Laboratory and simulation training allow students to develop technical skills in imaging equipment operation, patient positioning, and diagnostic imaging procedures.

The final year focuses on advanced imaging practice and extensive supervised clinical training in hospitals and diagnostic imaging departments. Through these experiences, students gain hands-on exposure to real clinical cases and multidisciplinary healthcare teams. Graduates develop the technical competence, analytical thinking, and professional confidence required to contribute to high-quality diagnostic imaging services and patient-centered healthcare.

Bachelor of Science in Optometry - Dubai Medical University - College of Health Sciences

The Bachelor of Science in Optometry (BS-OPT) at Dubai Medical University is a four-year program designed to prepare primary eye-care professionals capable of examining vision, detecting ocular disorders, and supporting the prevention and management of visual impairment. The program integrates strong foundations in biomedical sciences with specialized training in optical science, vision assessment, ocular health, and clinical optometric practice.

During the first two years, students build essential knowledge in biology, chemistry, physics, anatomy and physiology, microbiology, and pharmacology, while developing professional competencies in communication, research, and healthcare ethics. Students are introduced to the fundamentals of optometry, including geometrical and visual optics, ocular anatomy and physiology, and the principles of optometric examination and binocular vision. Laboratory sessions provide hands-on training in visual optics and basic clinical assessment techniques.

In Year 3, the curriculum advances into specialized optometric topics such as ophthalmic lenses and dispensing, diagnostic instrumentation, ocular diseases, ocular pharmacology, visual perception, and optometric care across different age groups. Practical laboratories strengthen students’ clinical examination skills and their ability to use diagnostic equipment and vision assessment technologies.

The final year focuses on advanced optometric practice and extensive supervised clinical training in eye-care clinics and healthcare settings. Students also study areas such as contact lenses, community eye care, myopia management, and low-vision rehabilitation. Through these experiences, graduates develop the technical competence, clinical reasoning, and professional confidence required to deliver high-quality vision care and contribute to multidisciplinary healthcare teams.

BPharm Program Overview

The Bachelor of Pharmacy program at Dubai Medical University spans four and half years with 160 credit hours. It combines foundational sciences, pharmaceutical studies, professional skills, and experiential practice.

Years 1–2 build a base in biomedical sciences: anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, microbiology, and pharmaceutics. General education in communication, technology, psychology, and culture is integrated. Early exposure to pharmacy includes law, ethics, and public health. Laboratory sessions reinforce theoretical knowledge with practical skills.
By Year 2, students complete Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience I in community pharmacies.

Years 3–4 focus on integrated pharmacotherapy modules blending pathophysiology, pharmacology, chemistry, and therapy. Supporting subjects include pharmacokinetics, pharmacoeconomics, pharmacovigilance, genetics, and immunology. Case-based learning and simulations enhance decision-making and teamwork skills. Hospital-based IPPE II follows in Year 3. Electives allow exploration of specialized pharmacy or science topics. Graduates emerge as competent pharmacists, prepared for licensure and diverse healthcare, academic, regulatory, or industry roles.

DMU College of Nursing, Master of Science in Critical Care Nursing Program

The Master of Science in Critical Care Nursing (MS-CC) at Dubai Medical University is a two-year graduate program designed to prepare registered nurses for advanced clinical practice and leadership in the care of critically ill adults. The program responds to the growing demand for nurses with specialized expertise in complex and rapidly changing physiological conditions, advanced patient assessment, clinical decision-making, life-support technologies, and coordinated care across high-acuity healthcare environments.

The curriculum integrates advanced health assessment, pathophysiology, clinical pharmacology, critical care nursing theory, evidence-based practice, and research. Students complete 400 supervised clinical hours across two critical care nursing practicum courses, enabling them to apply advanced clinical reasoning, respond to acute and life-threatening conditions, collaborate effectively with interprofessional teams, and support patients and families throughout complex critical illness.

Research preparation is embedded throughout the program through advanced research methods, data management and analysis, and a master’s thesis. Graduates will be equipped to improve the quality and safety of critical care, lead practice-development and quality-improvement initiatives, contribute to healthcare policy and professional education, and advance nursing scholarship in the UAE and the wider region.

History of College Of Medicine - founders Message

More than 30 years ago, establishing a world-renowned medical education institution for girls in the UAE would seem like an impossible dream. Yet, on August 1, 1986, our founder Haj Saeed bin Ahmed Al Lootah accomplished that very goal and classes began at DMU College of Medicine with Professor Dr. Zahira H. Abdin as the founding dean. His visionary dream had become a reality.

During these formative years, the College received substantial professional support and advice from the Leicester Medical School in the United Kingdom and the Cairo Medical School in Egypt. This international contribution combined with the faculty's extensive experience led to the creation of an intensive curriculum that would incorporate the best of the world's medical practices.

Since its inception, College of Medicine has been fortunate to receive help from the government of Dubai's Department of Health and Medical Services under its former Director H.E. Dr. Juma Khalfan Balhoul. The departments hospitals opened their doors and welcomed College of Medicine (COM) students for clinical training. Our continued drive for excellence demands seamless integration between clinical and pre-clinical phases. In 2004, a Memorandum of Understanding was signed by DHA and COM to secure this process.

What we now know, as an outstanding educational institution, is a product of the cooperative solidarity of a group of people who put their heart and soul into it. Three decades of academic distinction have made College of Medicine a truly dynamic center of higher education par excellence.

With over 1500 graduates practicing medicine across the world and a campus that includes professors and students from over 50 different countries, DMCG has earned a reputation as one of the best institutions for medical education and a beacon of academic excellence.
In September 2022, the College ownership was transferred under "Saeed Ahmad Lootah Charity Foundation".

The Student Success Center (SSC) at the College of Pharmacy is dedicated to supporting students throughout their academic journey and fostering their personal and professional development. As a central hub for student support, the SSC provides a welcoming environment where students can seek guidance on academic, personal, and university-related matters.

The SSC works proactively to promote student success by monitoring attendance and academic progress, identifying students who may benefit from additional support, and collaborating closely with faculty members, academic departments, and university services. Through timely interventions, personalized guidance, and student-centered initiatives, the SSC helps students overcome challenges, remain engaged in their studies, and achieve their full potential.

Academic Integrity and Student Conduct
Academic mentorship is an integral part of our student support system, providing students with continuous academic guidance, personalized support, and encouragement throughout their studies.

Every student is assigned a faculty mentor to provide ongoing academic guidance and support. Faculty mentors meet regularly with students to discuss academic performance, assist with academic planning, monitor academic progress, help them set academic and professional goals, and address any personal or academic challenges that may affect their success. They also support students in adjusting to university life, making informed academic decisions, understanding university requirements, and accessing appropriate university resources when needed.

The Student Success Center works closely with students, faculty mentors, and the Associate Dean for Academic Affairs to identify challenges and develop effective strategies for academic success. Through continuous mentoring, personalized support, early intervention, and collaborative support, the SSC and faculty mentors help students stay on track, achieve their academic goals, and make the most of their university experience.

The Learning Enhancement and Peer Support (LEAP) Program is a structured, student-led peer tutoring initiative at the COP. LEAP fosters a collaborative and inclusive learning environment where students support one another in strengthening their understanding of course material, developing effective study strategies, and building confidence in their learning.

LEAP tutors are selected through a structured, merit-based process and receive formal training in effective tutoring practices, communication skills, learning strategies, professionalism, and academic integrity before supporting their peers. Working under faculty supervision, they provide high-quality academic support while promoting ethical and collaborative learning.

The program offers a variety of learning formats, including one-to-one tutoring, small-group tutoring, study sessions, and workshops. Through LEAP, students receive guidance from trained peer tutors who help reinforce key concepts, improve study habits, develop critical thinking skills, and enhance overall academic success. At the same time, the program provides peer tutors with valuable opportunities to develop leadership, communication, teaching, and professional skills.

The SSC manages student attendance records and reviews absence excuses in learning and assessment sessions, in accordance with university policies. By maintaining accurate records, the SSC helps students stay on track with their studies and ensures transparency in attendance monitoring.

Attendance alerts are issued regularly to students whose attendance falls below the required threshold, and faculty mentors are informed to facilitate timely follow-up, guidance, and support. Through proactive attendance monitoring and early intervention, the SSC helps students remain engaged in their studies and maintain satisfactory academic progress.

The SSC provides students with a fair, transparent, and supportive process to raise concerns and seek resolution for academic matters. Students are encouraged to resolve concerns informally whenever possible by discussing the matter with the relevant faculty or staff member. If the issue cannot be resolved, a formal grievance or appeal may be submitted through the Student Voice Form.

The SSC guides students throughout the process, ensuring that grievances and appeals are reviewed in accordance with University policies and referred to the appropriate individuals or committees when required. Students are informed of the outcome through the University's established procedures. If they are dissatisfied with the outcome of a grievance, they may submit an appeal in accordance with the University's Grievances and Appeals Policy.

Students are also encouraged to submit suggestions through the Student Voice Form to enhance academic programs, student services, university facilities, and the overall student experience. Student feedback is highly valued and plays an important role in supporting the University's commitment to continuous quality improvement.

The Student Success Center (SSC) at the College of Nursing serves as a central hub for student support and guidance. It is designed to support students throughout their academic journey and personal growth by providing a supportive environment where they can seek assistance with academic, personal, or university-related concerns.

The SSC monitors student attendance and academic progress, identifies students who may require additional support, and works closely with students, faculty, academic programs, and university services to help students overcome challenges, stay engaged, and succeed in their studies. Through its various services, the SSC ensures that every student receives the guidance, assistance, and motivation needed to achieve academic success and personal development. These are in line with the UAE's strategic direction of promoting happiness and positivity.

The Student Success Center (SSC) is committed to supporting students throughout their academic journey by regularly monitoring academic progress and identifying students who may be at risk of academic difficulty. Through early intervention and personalized support, the SSC works closely with students, faculty mentors, and Associate Dean for Academic Affairs to identify challenges and develop effective strategies for academic success.

As part of this support system, every student is assigned a faculty mentor who provides individualized academic guidance throughout their studies. Faculty mentors regularly monitor students' progress, meet with them to discuss academic performance, assist with academic planning, and help address any personal or academic challenges that may affect their success. They also support students in adjusting to university life, making informed academic decisions, and accessing appropriate university resources when needed.

Through continuous mentoring, early intervention, and collaborative support, the SSC and faculty mentors help students stay on track, achieve their academic goals, and make the most of their university experience.

The SSC organizes peer tutoring programs designed to create an inclusive learning community where students support each other in strengthening their understanding of course material and developing effective study strategies.

Peer tutoring at DMU is delivered through structured, student-led initiatives under faculty supervision. The program is offered in a variety of learning formats, including one-to-one tutoring, small-group tutoring, study sessions, and workshops.
Senior or high-achieving students support their colleagues in understanding challenging subjects, strengthening their knowledge, improving study habits, and building confidence in their learning.
Attendance alerts are sent regularly to students, and academic mentors are kept informed of attendance concerns to facilitate timely follow-up and support when needed.

Students may sometimes face issues related to their academic or university experience. The SSC provides a clear process to submit grievances or appeals in a safe and fair environment. This ensures that student concerns are heard and addressed according to DMU policies. The SSC also guides students through the process and directs them to the appropriate individuals or committees when needed.

The SSC promotes a culture of academic integrity, professionalism, and responsible conduct among students. The SSC provides guidance on university policies and supports students in understanding and meeting the expectations of the DMU community.

The SSC also supports the implementation of the Student Misconduct and Academic Integrity Policy by assisting with the reporting, documentation, and follow-up of cases in accordance with university procedures. Students may seek guidance from the SSC regarding academic integrity and student conduct matters at any stage of the process.

Nursing Simulation Center
Nursing Simulation Center at Dubai Medical University

The Nursing Simulation Center at Dubai Medical University's College of Nursing provides students with an innovative, technology-enhanced learning environment that bridges classroom knowledge with real-world clinical practice. Designed to replicate authentic healthcare settings, our laboratories offer structured, hands-on, and simulation-based learning experiences that prepare students to deliver safe, competent, and patient-centered care.

Equipped with high-, medium-, and low-fidelity patient simulators, advanced task trainers, immersive learning technologies, and authentic clinical equipment, the labs allow students to practiceessential nursing skills in a safe and supportive environment before entering clinical placements.

Through realistic simulation scenarios, students develop clinical competence, critical thinking, communication, teamwork, clinical judgment, and decision-making skills while building the confidence required to excel in diverse healthcare settings.
